title: Twenty-Six

lines.text: Reno, Nevada. August 2016. A woman in her seventies is admitted with an infected hip.
lines.spoken: Reno, Nevada. August, twenty sixteen. A woman in her seventies is admitted with an infected hip.
lines.hero: the date and place, set big; then a hospital wristband card, no name

lines.text: Her doctors do what doctors always do. They reach for antibiotics.
lines.spoken: Her doctors do what doctors always do. They reach for antibiotics.
lines.hero: a row of antibiotic cards dealt onto the board, face down

lines.text: The hospital tests fourteen. Not one of them works.
lines.spoken: The hospital tests fourteen. Not one of them works.
lines.hero: counter rolls to 14; RESISTANT stamps on 'works'

lines.text: The samples go to the CDC. They try twenty-six. Every single one fails.
lines.spoken: The samples go to the C D C. They try twenty-six. Every single one fails.
lines.hero: counter rolls on to 26; the whole row turns red on 'fails'

lines.text: In September, she dies. From an infection we once knew how to cure.
lines.spoken: In September, she dies. From an infection we once knew how to cure.
lines.hero: the CDC report itself (MMWR page), 'pan-resistant' highlighted

lines.text: Twenty-six.
lines.spoken: Twenty-six.
lines.hero: title, set huge, on black

lines.text: Seventy-one years earlier, in 1945, the man who discovered penicillin accepted the Nobel Prize.
lines.spoken: Seventy-one years earlier, in nineteen forty-five, the man who discovered penicillin accepted the Nobel Prize.
lines.hero: archive portrait of Alexander Fleming in his lab

lines.text: He could have simply celebrated. Instead, he warned us.
lines.spoken: He could have simply celebrated. Instead, he warned us.
lines.hero: his Nobel lecture page slides in beside the portrait

lines.text: Expose microbes to too little of the drug, he said, and you make them resistant.
lines.spoken: Expose microbes to too little of the drug, he said, and you make them resistant.
lines.hero: the lecture page: highlighter sweeps his real sentence, landing on 'resistant'

lines.text: We heard him. And we did it anyway.
lines.spoken: We heard him. And we did it anyway.
lines.hero: pull back: the lecture page small and alone

lines.text: Antibiotics for a cold, which is a virus they cannot touch.
lines.spoken: Antibiotics for a cold, which is a virus they cannot touch.
lines.hero: card: COLD = VIRUS

lines.text: Tablets bought over the counter, without a prescription.
lines.spoken: Tablets bought over the counter, without a prescription.
lines.hero: card: NO PRESCRIPTION

lines.text: Leftover strips, shared with family. Courses stopped halfway.
lines.spoken: Leftover strips, shared with family. Courses stopped halfway.
lines.hero: card: HALF A STRIP

lines.text: Tonnes given to healthy farm animals, just to make them grow faster.
lines.spoken: Tonnes given to healthy farm animals, just to make them grow faster.
lines.hero: card: FARMS

lines.text: Every careless dose is a lesson. And bacteria learn fast.
lines.spoken: Every careless dose is a lesson. And bacteria learn fast.
lines.hero: red string draws from every card to the 26 row

lines.text: In 2021, drug-resistant infections directly killed more than a million people.
lines.spoken: In twenty twenty-one, drug-resistant infections directly killed more than a million people.
lines.hero: counter rolls to 1,140,000

lines.text: That is more than HIV. More than malaria.
lines.spoken: That is more than H I V. More than malaria.
lines.hero: three bars side by side; AMR's is tallest

lines.text: By 2050, the forecast is thirty-nine million more lives lost.
lines.spoken: By twenty fifty, the forecast is thirty-nine million more lives lost.
lines.hero: counter rolls to 39,000,000

lines.text: The world has just marked World AMR Awareness Week.
lines.spoken: The world has just marked World A M R Awareness Week.
lines.hero: card: the week's dates and theme

lines.text: It is easy to scroll past. Another week. Another guideline.
lines.spoken: It is easy to scroll past. Another week. Another guideline.
lines.hero: the card starts to slide off the board

lines.text: But she was not a guideline. She was a person, in a modern hospital, with nothing left to try.
lines.spoken: But she was not a guideline. She was a person, in a modern hospital, with nothing left to try.
lines.hero: camera returns to the wristband card from line one

lines.text: The next patient with no options could be someone you love.
lines.spoken: The next patient with no options could be someone you love.
lines.hero: the empty space beside the wristband

lines.text: Ask if you really need it. Take it exactly as prescribed. Never share it.
lines.spoken: Ask if you really need it. Take it exactly as prescribed. Never share it.
lines.hero: three short cards, one per sentence

lines.text: Twenty-six antibiotics failed her. Let's keep the next one working.
lines.spoken: Twenty-six antibiotics failed her. Let's keep the next one working.
lines.hero: final pull-back: the whole board; one antibiotic card left face up, glowing

fact_notes: Lines 1-5: CDC MMWR 66(1):33, 13 Jan 2017, 'Notes from the Field: Pan-Resistant NDM-Producing Klebsiella pneumoniae, Washoe County, Nevada, 2016' (https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/66/wr/mm6601a7.htm). Woman in her 70s, admitted mid-August 2016 in Reno with SIRS from an infected right hip seroma; isolate resistant to 26 antibiotics on CDC testing (14 on the hospital panel); died early September 2016 of septic shock. Patient is never named or pictured.

Line 4: the 26 includes all aminoglycosides and polymyxins tested; tigecycline was 'intermediate', not fully resistant. 'Every single one fails' = every drug available in the US was ineffective, per MMWR / NPR coverage. Keep wording or soften to 'every one was useless' if a reviewer objects.
She had earlier been hospitalised in India for a femur fracture; deliberately left out of the script to avoid blaming a country. Message is 'bacteria cross borders'.

Lines 7-9: Fleming, Nobel Lecture 'Penicillin', 11 Dec 1945 (nobelprize.org). Real sentence to highlight on screen: 'the ignorant man may easily underdose himself and by exposing his microbes to non-lethal quantities of the drug make them resistant.' Line 9 is a paraphrase in narration only; the screen shows his exact words. The popular 'Mr. X' parable is NOT used: could not verify its source.
Line 13: 'courses stopped halfway' — WHO guidance remains 'take as prescribed'.
Line 14: animal use is part of the One Health theme (WHO/FAO/UNEP/WOAH).
Line 16: GRAM / Lancet 2024 (Naghavi et al.): 1.14 million deaths attributable to bacterial AMR in 2021; 4.71 million associated.

Line 17: GRAM / Lancet 2022 (Murray et al.) for 2019: AMR 1.27M attributable vs HIV ~864k and malaria ~643k. 2021 HIV and malaria deaths were also below 1.14M (UNAIDS ~650k; WHO World Malaria Report ~619k).
Line 18: GRAM / Lancet 2024 forecast: 39 million attributable deaths cumulatively 2025-2050; 1.91 million a year by 2050.
Line 19: World AMR Awareness Week 2026, 18-24 November; theme 'One Health, one action: Prevent AMR now' (WHO campaign page).
